activities.description: Expert greets the viewers and introduces the question from Greg in Poland.
Expert begins explaining the difference between coated abrasives and non-woven pads.
Expert shows a piece of coated abrasive (grade 180) and a non-woven pad (also grade 180).
Expert explains that the coated abrasive is a 'monolayer product' where the abrasive grains are pushed into the surface of the metal.
Expert explains that non-woven products have a 'sponge effect' and act like a spring, meaning the grit will not penetrate into the metal as hard as a monolayer product.
Expert uses the analogy of a car's suspension to explain how non-woven products work.
Expert shows a flat disc (grit 80) and a non-woven product (grade 'coarse') to further illustrate the difference in material removal.
Expert concludes the explanation and encourages viewers to leave more questions in the comments.

Okay, so this is what we would call quite a fine sandpaper when we use this as on a surface, such as this here to sand down.

youtube_description:
Non-woven abrasives products are made from nylon fibers impregnated with abrasive grains. These are the same grains as you'd find in a coated abrasive product, so you'd be right to assume they use the same grit description. 

As Paul our Application Engineer explains, this isn't the case and that's because in a coated abrasive (where the grit is applied to a backing such as paper or cloth), when applied with pressure to a surface, the grain is pushed into it, which cuts through the material as there's nowhere else for the grain to go. This is known as a mono-layer product and the term 'grit size' is used.

With non-woven, the nylon gives a sponge effect, like a spring, which allows the abrasive to push back from the surface. This means the grain isn't applied so aggressively to the metal, even if it's the same grit, giving a softer finish. Non-wovens use the term 'grade' instead of grit to describe their aggression.

Coated abrasives will always remove more material than non-wovens, so (depending on the job), use a coated abrasive first, followed by the non-woven for optimum results. 

If you'd like to challenge our Norton expert, feel free to drop a question in the comments box below and we'll get back to you with an answer. 

For more information about Norton abrasives, or how we can help you, visit https://www.nortonabrasives.com/en-gb or contact your local distributor.
